interestReview.finding: All 33 exact-target rows re-read and reconciled with current source content: 14 generator,9 support,10 search-only. Nine generator rows are owned by the broad media/public core; four digital/AI rows generate option 2; organisational messaging generates option 3. academicJudgment.claim: The verified communication/media and social-research curriculum supports three meaningful broader UCR responses with public/cultural, computational/digital and organisational/consumer emphases; the specialist communication-science and required practical/culminating gaps remain explicit.
academicJudgment.strongestResponse: The closest option contains sustained film/media analysis and production, rhetorical/persuasive communication, social/cultural theory and actual empirical methods. Its specific applied extensions concern public debate, youth media literacy, climate communication and organisations. It is broader than communication science, but is not an assortment justified merely by generic breadth.
academicJudgment.alternatives: The second option replaces five courses with programming, mathematics, image processing, neural networks and institutional AI study. The third replaces six with leadership/organisational psychology, negotiation, marketing, digital strategy and international business. Both retain the actual media and empirical foundation. Pairwise differences are 5,6,8 courses (37.5,45,60 EC each).
academicJudgment.limits: Dedicated comparative media systems, international/global communication, the staged field-specific quantitative/research workshops, a required field internship and required empirical thesis are not reproduced. The available taught media/rhetorical/social-methods core is sufficiently substantial for a broader positive comparison; optional research supplies no missing taught discipline.

adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: External research preparation is stronger. UCR still supplies sustained media/persuasion inquiry and actual quantitative, qualitative, documentary and audience research; no workshop equivalence or complete research sequence is claimed.

courseReview.finding: All 35 selected current course identities, available descriptions/profiles, relevant topics/methods and hard planning facts were examined. Every non-PPD course has a specific trace. Historical outlines supply content, not future offerings. Market Research, Strategy & Digital Transformation and Communicating the Climate Crisis are used only within their descriptions. HCBPSYC315 is a concrete media-literacy/counter-narrative contribution, not a generic psychology filler. Mathematics and programming supply the included computational image/text courses, not an unsupported mathematical strand.
courseReview.progression: First-year media, rhetoric and sociology precede advanced media/social study. Statistics precedes leadership survey/organisational study; the business gateway precedes market research and strategy. Digital option programming precedes image processing; Mathematical Methods precedes Neural Networks. All three keep exactly24courses, six terms, year-one PPD and at least six advanced courses.

alignmentReview.finding: Each of 35 distinct UCR codes owns one row/block, shared only by code. All25external components occur once at supported weights. Direct subject/method relationships include moving-image study, social foundations, public spheres, media-technology history, AI social effects, statistics, qualitative inquiry, documentary production and leadership communication.
alignmentReview.challenge: The external theory of international media systems, industry/audience overview, dedicated intercultural study and staged field-specific methods retain separate rows. A broad 10-EC focus package is not divided into invented courses or aligned to one UCR subject. PPD is not aligned to labour-market orientation. UCR projects do not become the required internship. Optional15ECresearch is outside all180ECschedules, parallel to the documented thesis and never proof of eligibility.

sourceFirstChallenge.method: Separately identified second pass by the same AI. Began again from OER/TER learning outcomes, new-cohort Appendix8 and Articles4.5/A11.3, then actual UCR taught media/rhetoric/social-research and computational/business content, then the finished comparison. This is not independent human or separate-agent review.
sourceFirstChallenge.positiveChallenge: The external programme is not only culture or content-making: it includes communication theory, international comparison, quantitative and qualitative research, organisations and practice. The UCR claim is accepted because it sustains actual media/persuasion and empirical inquiry with specific conceptual responses, while explicitly acknowledging missing specialist sequences and required practice. Broad business courses alone would fail.
sourceFirstChallenge.uncertaintyChallenge: An extra research workshop strengthens an already verified research strand; embedded-workshop or another allocation correction changes formal/local weight; stricter entry changes eligibility. None removes the independently established subjects or reverses the precise broader UCR claim. No percentage rule or assumed five-credit tolerance is used.
sourceFirstChallenge.alternativeChallenge: Digital maths/programming are foundations for actual selected image/text methods. Organisational psychology/negotiation/marketing are a different substantive route, not arbitrary substitutions. All interest directions are accounted for before course selection.
sourceFirstChallenge.correctionsDuringVerification: Added the explicit official-order neutral-route enum, corrected pairwise differences to5/6/8, and reconciled every trace basis with its alternative. No academic gate or validator was weakened.
sourceFirstChallenge.result: The qualified limited claim survives; source uncertainty remains explicit and no robust no-match is inferred.
